headline: ICT prosecution submits charge against 7 AL leaders over July uprising
summary: Former ministers and a top adviser face allegations of crimes against humanity for allegedly implementing a state policy to suppress the 2024 protests.
details: The prosecution has submitted a formal charge to the International Crimes Tribunal (ICT) against seven Awami League leaders for alleged crimes against humanity during the July 2024 uprising.
The accused include former ministers Amir Hossain Amu, Abdur Razzaque, Shahjahan Khan, Dipu Moni, Mirza Azam, and Faruk Khan, along with former energy adviser Taufiq-e-Elahi Chowdhury.
Six of the named leaders are currently in jail, while Mirza Azam remains absconding, according to the prosecution.
Prosecutor Gazi Monawar Hossain Tamim stated that the accused allegedly helped plan, facilitate, and implement a state policy to suppress the uprising.
The prosecution claims the then-government adopted the suppression of the movement as state policy, with the Awami League and 14-party alliance making political decisions to crush it.
As influential policymakers, the accused allegedly participated in and contributed to the crackdown on protesters.
Evidence submitted to the tribunal includes recordings of conversations involving former PM Sheikh Hasina and the accused, as well as a UN fact-finding report on the July uprising.
caption:
Seven top Awami League leaders now face formal charges of crimes against humanity at the ICT.

The prosecution has submitted a formal charge to the International Crimes Tribunal (ICT) against seven Awami League leaders for alleged crimes against humanity during the July 2024 uprising.

The accused include former ministers Amir Hossain Amu, Abdur Razzaque, Shahjahan Khan, Dipu Moni, Mirza Azam, and Faruk Khan, along with former energy adviser Taufiq-e-Elahi Chowdhury.

Six of the named leaders are currently in jail, while Mirza Azam remains absconding, according to the prosecution.

Prosecutor Gazi Monawar Hossain Tamim stated that the accused allegedly helped plan, facilitate, and implement a state policy to suppress the uprising.

The prosecution claims the then-government adopted the suppression of the movement as state policy, with the Awami League and 14-party alliance making political decisions to crush it.

As influential policymakers, the accused allegedly participated in and contributed to the crackdown on protesters.

Evidence submitted to the tribunal includes recordings of conversations involving former PM Sheikh Hasina and the accused, as well as a UN fact-finding report on the July uprising.

headline_marked: Lawmaker's son [[placed on fresh two-day remand]] for Shakil murder
headline: Lawmaker's son placed on fresh two-day remand for Shakil murder
summary: Nuruzzaman Mintu, son of Natore-4 lawmaker Md Abdul Aziz, faces further police interrogation in the death of JCD leader Shakil Islam.
details: A court has placed Nuruzzaman Mintu, the son of Natore-4 lawmaker Md Abdul Aziz, on a fresh two-day police remand. This action follows his arrest on October 27 for alleged involvement in the murder of JCD leader Shakil Islam.
Shakil Islam, 30, died in Dhaka on October 26 after sustaining injuries from an attack that occurred on October 14.
Natore Detective Branch (DB) investigators had sought a five-day remand, but the court granted two days for further interrogation.

The case has sparked protests demanding the lawmaker's expulsion from the party. Natore district BNP Secretary Md Asaduzzaman stated that disciplinary action rests with the party's central leadership.
Lawmaker Md Abdul Aziz has denied any involvement by himself or his family members, describing the allegations as a 'conspiracy'.
caption:

Natore Detective Branch (DB) investigators had sought a five-day remand, but the court granted two days for further interrogation.

The case has sparked protests demanding the lawmaker's expulsion from the party. Natore district BNP Secretary Md Asaduzzaman stated that disciplinary action rests with the party's central leadership.

Lawmaker Md Abdul Aziz has denied any involvement by himself or his family members, describing the allegations as a 'conspiracy'.
